distress._note: Author-written, NOT native-reviewed and NOT clinically reviewed (docs/knowledge/distress-handoff.md). Texts are matched after NFKC, casefold, accent strip and apostrophe removal ('dont', 'im'), so write fragments in that folded form. A cue is a closed-vocabulary sequence (seq: group names joined by the closed `fillers`) or a plain regex (re). `negatable` cues drop to the gentle tier when a negation word sits just before them. Over-triggering is preferred to missing: every guard only ever lowers handoff to gentle, never to none, except `idioms`.

restraint._note: Restraint (restraint.py): the words a row / thread / turn is judged sensitive by, the 'what's up?' pull phrases and the spoken-mute grammar. Fragments are regex alternatives; mute_patterns are whole regexes over the normalised utterance (restraint_lex.norm). A PRE-FILTER that can only WITHHOLD. English is byte-for-byte what restraint.py hard-coded before (tests/test_restraint_lexicon.py).

commitments._note: The words of ZOE'S OWN timed promises (commitments.py, ZOE_COMMITMENTS): the first-person future cues she uses ('I'll remind you', 'I'll check back'), the guards that make a sentence an offer or a condition instead, the clock/day/part-of-day words that give a promise its due time, and the sentences she says when she owns one up. Regex fragments, matched case-insensitively. Only ZOE's reply is ever read with these - never the user's words.

_note_change_cues: night_mind.change_backed: a moment the model labels kind=change only changes a thread's status (or retires its earlier observations) when its own words carry one of these cues or an ended_verbs / ended_phrases marker. Model points, code decides (K9f flat-week false notices).
_note_clause_joiners: night_mind.moment_change_backed: words that start a new clause inside one sentence (punctuation , ; : and dashes also split). A change cue backs a moment only from the clause(s) its quote overlaps, so another subject's 'now lives' in the same sentence is not borrowed.

manner.block: Talk like a friend, not a counsellor. Never open with "It sounds like", "That sounds like" or "I hear you", and never restate what they just said. Start with something of your own: a fact, a real opinion, a related thought, a next step. If they are upset, one short clause is enough ("Ugh, rough."), then carry on. Ask at most one question, only if the answer changes what you say next; otherwise end on a statement. If they criticise you, take it as feedback about you: name the exact thing, say what you will do. Never repeat your last answer. Never flatter.

mirror._note: mirror_guard.py: the reflective-listening formulas a reply may OPEN with (the 4B's default empathy tic: 'It sounds like you're ...'). Matched on lower-cased, accent-stripped WORDS at a sentence start, after any leading filler. Data, never code: a language with no entry here gets no guard (inert), it is never guessed from English.
generic_closers: how does that make you feel
how did that make you feel
do you want to talk about it
would you like to talk about it
what can i do to help
would you like to tell me more

risk_cues._note: The risk-cue tier (risk_cues.py, ZOE_RISK_CUES): CODE finds the problem in a plan the user just announced and hands the brain ONE short note naming it, so the 4B only has to voice the flaw, not find it. Regex fragments, matched case-insensitively against the user's own words after apostrophes are normalised to '. plan.* decide whether the turn is an announced plan at all. cues[]: every pattern in 'all' must match and no pattern in 'absent' may; {0} {1} in 'note' are filled with the words each 'all' pattern matched. timing.* is the clock arithmetic (two things at one time; too little lead before a flight). Categories: safety_health, money_contract, irreversible, prerequisite, timing. Written from the categories of everyday life, not from any bench sentence. Only the user's words are ever read with these, never Zoe's reply.
risk_cues.heading: ## Before you answer, check
risk_cues.rule: Mention the concern once, briefly and kindly, then help with the plan. Do not lecture, refuse or repeat it.

cues.note: Safety: the plan says "{0}" and they also said "{1}" - that combination is risky.
Safety: they mentioned "{0}" and also plan "{1}" - it may be too much for it.
Safety: they plan on "{0}", which is the usual protection against getting hurt.
Health: they plan on "{0}" - a change like that is safest checked with their doctor or pharmacist first.
Health: that meal ("{0}") is mostly sugar or caffeine; it will not keep them going for long.
Health: that meal ("{0}") has no protein or anything filling in it.
Health: "{0}" for that long is hard on the body.
Money: the plan says "{0}" with "{1}" - everything in one place, nothing kept back.
Money: "{1}" is never a guarantee in a bet or investment ("{0}").
Money: they plan "{0}" while "{1}" - how the bills get paid is still unanswered.
Contract: they plan "{0}" "{1}" - an unread contract is hard to undo.
Money: paying "{0}" to someone met through "{1}" is the usual shape of a scam.
Money: handing over "{0}" after contact from "{1}" is how scams work; a real bank never asks.
Irreversible: "{0}" cannot be undone, and no backup was mentioned.
Irreversible: "{0}" erases everything on it, and no backup was mentioned.
Irreversible: the message has "{1}" in it, and a message cannot be taken back once sent.
Irreversible: "{1}" is hard to take back, and they said "{0}" - sleeping on it would cost nothing.
Missing piece: they said "{0}" and the plan may depend on it.
Missing piece: they said they "{0}" - something the plan needs is still undone.
Missing piece: they plan "{0}" but "{1}" - the people it affects do not know yet.

timing.tight: Timing: the {0} against the {1} leaves only {2} minutes, which is too tight.
timing.late: Timing: the {1} is at or after the {0}, so they would miss it.
timing.double: Timing: two things are set for the same time ("{0}" and "{1}").

_note_present_verbs: Bare present-tense verbs: a word after a coordinator under "User" is conjugated into second person ("likes tea but hates coffee" -> "like tea but hate coffee") ONLY when it is one of these in its third-person form AND an object follows, so a plural noun ("tea and cats") is never taken for a verb.

memory_challenge._note: The user CHALLENGES Zoe's memory (memory_gate.is_memory_challenge): 'don't you remember', 'you already know', 'we've already talked about it', 'I told you about that' - but NOT plain past conversation ('we talked to the electrician and he fixed the fuse'): "we talked" needs 'already', 'before', 'earlier' or an anaphoric 'about it/this/that'. Such a turn is a recall question whatever its grammar: the seam runs a recall pass first, and the brain is told to answer only from what comes back. Regex fragments, matched case-insensitively against the user's words with apostrophes normalised to '.

spacer._note: voice_spacer.py: the short spoken lines that fill a wait. 'families' are the pools by what the turn is doing (lookup = a read of stored data, recall = remembering, action = doing something, generic = nothing known); 'tool_ack' is the domain-specific pool for the dispatch-time acknowledgement. A line never claims a result. Wide on purpose: the same three lines on every turn read as a tic.

recall: Let me see what I remember.

calendar: Let me look at your calendar.
lists: Let me look at your lists.
reminders: Let me look at your reminders.
weather: Let me look at the weather.

wellbeing._note: conversation_cues.py: a question about HOW ZOE IS (or small talk aimed at her) is conversation, never a canned greeting and never a private request. 'patterns' = wellbeing questions; 'small_talk' = other chat aimed at Zoe; 'frames' = the lead-in a person puts in front of it ('I want to know how you are'), removed before the privacy check; 'examples' = rows the tests run through every consumer.
examples: I want to know how you are
I just want to know how you are doing
can I ask how you are

turn_continuation._note: conversation_cues.turn_continuation: a short CONTEXT-FREE continuation ('what else', 'and?', 'tell me more', 'anything else', 'go on'). It carries no topic of its own, so it follows the previous turn's domain (same panel, recent window) instead of being routed by its own meaningless embedding. The WHOLE utterance (after 'lead_ins' and 'fillers' are taken off both ends) must match one of 'patterns' (regex fragments, full match). A language with no section contributes nothing.
patterns: what else (?:is there|do you have|can you (?:tell|say)(?: me)?)
not_continuations: what else do you know about me
anything else on my calendar today

calendar_followup._note: conversation_cues.calendar_followup: a short question about the calendar answer Zoe JUST gave ('what is it', 'what are they', 'what's the one event', 'which one'). The WHOLE utterance (after 'lead_ins' and 'fillers' are taken off both ends) must match one of 'patterns' (regex fragments, full match). The caller supplies the freshness window and the member-scoped read; a language with no section contributes nothing.
patterns: (?:read|say) (?:it|them|that|those)(?: out| out loud| to me| again)?
examples: what's the one event on my calendar
I was wondering what the one event for today is
can you tell me what it is
not_followups: what is the capital of france
what is it like on mars
what is the one thing you like about music

smart_home_followup._note: conversation_cues.smart_home_followup: a bare pronoun command about the device just controlled ('turn it back on again' right after 'turn the light off'). The WHOLE utterance must be made of these words: 'verbs' + 'pronouns' + on/off/back, with 'fillers' ignored; a pronoun, or 'back' beside on/off, is required; 'back' with no on/off reverses the last action. 'self_contained' lists on/off words that already carry their object (a language that fuses the pronoun into the verb).
not_followups: put it on my shopping list
turn it back on and play jazz

command_filler._note: conversation_cues.strip_command_filler: politeness and wake words around a COMMAND (Home Assistant's skip words, sentences/en/_common.yaml, plus wake words). The deterministic matchers (skybridge_service, intent_router) retry WITHOUT them only when the words as said matched nothing, so a pattern that already matches is never changed. 'lead' fragments are stripped repeatedly from the start, 'tail' fragments from the end (regex fragments, case-insensitive, whole words; longer fragments first). The strip is abandoned when the word after a stripped lead is in 'not_after_lead': 'would you LIKE', 'can you HEAR me', 'can you REMEMBER' are questions or offers, not commands ('not_after_lead' entries are regex fragments). First-person leads ('I need to', 'I want to') are deliberately absent: 'I need to put the kids to bed' is a statement, and stripping it hands the loose add/remove patterns a command.

stripped.can you remind me to call the plumber to: remind me to call the plumber tomorrow

kept: would you like to hear a joke
can you remember what I said
could you tell me about your day

offer._note: conversation_cues.ends_with_offer: Zoe's last reply ENDS in an offer ('how about the history of coffee?'). A short acceptance ('sounds good') after one is an answer to the offer, so it goes to the brain with the conversation instead of the canned 'Okay.'. 'cues' are regexes on the last sentences of the reply; 'tail_chars' bounds how much of the end is read.
examples: Glad that helped. How about the history of coffee?
That's a lovely thought. Would you like to hear more?
I can also read you tomorrow's headlines, if you'd like.
Do you want me to look into it?
Want me to put that on your list?

voice_session._note: voice_session.py (ZOE_VOICE_SESSION): the words that LOCK or CLOSE a panel voice session, the phrases that still need a PIN inside one (step_up), the frames that make a request about ANOTHER member, and the panel/spoken texts. 'lock' and 'close' match the WHOLE normalised utterance (the 'strip' words removed from either end), never a fragment, so 'lock the front door' is not a lock. 'step_up' fragments are searched with word boundaries. 'other_member' templates carry {name}, replaced by each other member's escaped name. A language with no section locks nothing and steps nothing up by phrase (the intent and Skybridge tiers in voice_session_policy.json still apply).

voice_session.card_step_up: That needs your PIN, even when I know your voice.
voice_session.step_up_reason: That needs your PIN. Choose your profile and enter your PIN to continue.

mishear_clarify._note: mishear_clarify.py (flag ZOE_MISHEAR_CLARIFY): the light 'what was that?' lines Zoe speaks instead of answering a short, feeling-shaped line whose speech-to-text looks unreliable (a mishearing of a command as an affect line, 2026-10-14). 'phrases' = the clarification, ALL ending in a question mark (the panel daemon then opens its follow-up window and tags the repeat prev_reply_question). 'cues' = extra explicit-emotion words/regexes ON TOP of the restraint 'affect' list, the distress hand-off and the risk-cue tier: any hit means the line is a possible disclosure and is ALWAYS answered. 'a lot' is deliberately NOT a cue. A language with no entry here gets no guard (inert).
phrases: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Say again?
Sorry, could you say that again?
I missed that. One more time?
